text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like NVDA on 2026-09-18, the median realised return over the next 5 sessions was 0.86%. The distribution is wide and slightly right-skewed, with a 10th percentile of -4.04% and a 90th percentile of 4.68%, meaning the path can swing nearly 9 percentage points between bad and good outcomes in a single trading week.

[state]
The engine pulled these analogs because NVDA sits near its 52-week high (distance from 52-week high: -6.03%, z-score 0.564) while carrying elevated idiosyncratic risk: 20-session realised volatility is 45.77% (z-score 0.824) and mean absolute overnight/weekend gaps are 1.28% (z-score 0.718). Simultaneously, WTI crude surged 19.24% over 20 days (z-score 1.124), dollar volume is below average (20-session dollar-volume regime z-score: -0.62), and benchmark volatility is compressed at 9.16% (z-score -0.574). There are 45 calendar days to the next earnings release and 0 scheduled events in the next 5 sessions. Macro context shows a VIX level of 15.44, a 10y-2y Treasury slope of 0.25, and a Fed funds target change of 0.25 bp over 90 days. Equity market sentiment registers at 57.1 ("Greed") on the engine's internal gauge, though the CNN Business Fear & Greed cross-check reads 38.3 ("fear"), driven by extreme fear in stock price strength (0.8) and breadth (0.8). Per-symbol headlines from Yahoo Finance note that "Cerebras stock rises after Sam Altman calls it a 'close partner'" and that a low-cost Vanguard ETF has "32.4% Invested in Nvidia, Broadcom, Micron, AMD, Intel, and Lam Research." Crypto sentiment is a separate asset class reading 70 ("Greed") on alternative.me, relevant only to the tokenised wrapper context.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs, the mean 5-session return was 0.65% with a standard deviation of 3.8%. The distribution leans slightly positive (skew 0.214), ranging from a minimum of -7.34% to a maximum of 10.25%. In 56% of the episodes the return finished above zero, and in 44% it finished below. The bad tail is dominated by specific names: an XLK (Tech Select ETF) session on 2026-08-13 returned -4.02%, and the closest analog—an NVDA session on 2026-09-08—returned -5.9%. On the upside, an NVDA session on 2025-06-20 returned 9.66%. The retrieval set spans 31 distinct sessions across 33 symbols from 2016-12-14 to 2026-09-08, but is heavily concentrated in recent history, with 22 analogs from 2026 and 16 from 2025. Only 3 of the 50 analogs are NVDA itself.

[tails]
A position can end near flat and still be un-holdable mid-week. The median max adverse excursion across the 50 analogs was -2.01%, meaning the typical path dipped about 2% against the entry before recovering or settling. At the 10th percentile, the max adverse excursion reached -4.38%, and at the 25th percentile it was -3.77%. Conversely, the median max favourable excursion was 2.55%, reaching 6.71% at the 90th percentile, yielding a reward-to-risk ratio of 1.27. Looking at drawdown breaches specifically, 8% of the analog paths breached a 5% drawdown threshold during the 5-session horizon. None of the 50 paths breached a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown.

[stress]
The baseline median return is 0.86%. Under the "covid-crash" scenario (2020-02/03 liquidity crash), the median fell to -5.4% (a delta of -6.26%), with a 10th percentile of -14.14% and a 58.3% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns, making this a sample of one regime rather than a forecast. The "fed-tightening-2018" scenario dropped the median to -3.02% (delta -3.88%) with a 10th percentile of -6.18%; caveat: it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters late-window analogs. The "rate-shock-2022" scenario produced a median of -2.42% (delta -3.28%) and a 10th percentile of -8.44%; caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The "tariff-shock-2025" scenario yielded a median of -2.7% (delta -3.56%) using only 26 analogs; caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The "carry-unwind-2024" scenario showed a median of -2.11% (delta -2.97%); caveat: reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though intra-horizon excursion did not. The "liquidity-air-pocket" scenario barely moved the median to 0.83% (delta -0.03%), but its caveat is critical for this instrument: measured on NVDA/USDT (a Bitget RWA perpetual), the reference market is closed for 81.4% of the week and 54.59% of its realised hourly movement happened in those closed hours. The "earnings-day" scenario actually improved the median to 1.61% (delta 0.75%); caveat: earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. No scenarios were skipped.

[reasoning]
The three most relevant scenarios for a name near its highs with elevated idiosyncratic volatility are: first, the "covid-crash" scenario, because its median of -5.4% represents a -6.26% delta versus baseline across 48 analogs with a 58.3% breach probability, capturing what happens when diversification stops working. Second, the "rate-shock-2022" scenario, because its median of -2.42% (delta -3.28%) across 50 analogs directly targets multiple-rich names when stocks and bonds fall together. Third, the "liquidity-air-pocket" scenario, because while its median delta is only -0.03%, it explicitly addresses the 7x24 wrapper reality where 54.59% of movement occurs while the cash market is shut. A reader should distrust the heavy concentration of 2026 (22) and 2025 (16) analogs, as well as the fact that only 3 out of 50 are NVDA itself, meaning the set largely describes cross-sectional states rather than this specific ticker's history. The "earnings-day" scenario contradicts the cautious posture implied by the question, showing a positive median delta of 0.75% across 50 analogs, though the current state has 0 scheduled events in the next 5 sessions.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. As stated in the card's honestVerdict: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." The directional hit rate is 50.1%, and the conformal interval's matched coverage width (10.2%) is wider than the pooled unconditional benchmark (9.46%). For path risk validation, at the stated 10% drawdown level, the realised breach rate out of sample was 2%, while the mean predicted rate from the analog excursion share was 3.4%, producing a calibration gap of 1.4 percentage points with a clustered standard error of 0.48. The analog Brier score (MAE 0.0196) beat the vol-reflection benchmark (0.0241), the same-name calibration (0.024), and the pooled calibration (0.021). The paired Brier confidence intervals resolve all three comparisons, as 100% of bootstrap shares favoured the analog in each case and none spanned zero. The wrapper status is "measured" on the primary venue (Bitget official MCP, NVDA/USDT RWA perpetual futures). The reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 54.59% of the wrapper's realised hourly movement landed in those closed hours. It is a "fair tracker" with a return correlation of 0.8988 and a tracking error of 111 bp/day. The basis band is -0.37% to 0.66%, and the spread is 0.44 bps. Caveat: a fair perpetual is not the underlying; it carries idiosyncratic risk, funding applies, and the basis means exit prices differ from the reference close the analog distribution uses. For the return layer, measured across 6 weekend blocks, the median weekend block return was 0.428%, the 10th percentile was -1.3695%, and the standard deviation was 1.4103%. The median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.8185%, and 0% of weekends breached the 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions.
